outcomes: A CI job that is not Putnami's uploads its change evidence document to Putnami Cloud with a workspace token, or a GitHub Actions or gitlab.com CI job with its own ID token and no secret, or a person uploads it after signing in, and the run shows its tests, coverage, components, changed-line coverage and dependency changes, marked as self-reported, at the report URL the upload answers
nonGoals: Creating the observed workspace or its token: the runbook does it by hand for this slice
Keying the repository of a CI that names no numeric project id: a document without one is refused

requirements.text: putnami cloud evidence-report --file <path> reads a protocol/evidence v1 document and opens its run with POST /v1/delivery/records under the PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN bearer: the subject's provider, numeric project id as repo, commit and branch, the provenance of the CI, the pull or merge request as changeRequest, conclusion failure when a test failed, else success, and a submission id derived from the CI job, so a repeated upload opens no second run.

text: The provenance is gha for a github-actions document, gitlab for a gitlab-ci one and external for any other CI it names.
A generic document is external when the environment of the upload is a CI by the evidence protocol's markers, and local otherwise.
The run names its CI: ciSystem is the document's system, for a generic one the CI the environment's markers name;
runId, runAttempt and runUrl are the document's, runUrl without query or fragment. A local run sends none.
A member Delivery would refuse is left out with a warning: ciSystem putnami-ci or not short and lowercase, with the other three;
a run id over 128 characters, an attempt over 2147483647, a url not https without credentials or over 2048 characters, either with a space or control character.

The run carries under operational what the job tested, read with Git where the command was invoked: testedTree when the subject's commit is the merge the CI built (GitHub refs/pull/<n>/merge at GITHUB_SHA, a GitLab merged results or merge train pipeline at CI_COMMIT_SHA), else testedHeadTree;
with it, baselineMergeBase of the document's base and commit.
A value Git cannot compute is left out with a warning naming it and why.
A run refused for its operational opens again without it.

After the run, it posts the tests and coverage of each component in one batch to POST /v1/delivery/records/reports, then the components, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes, copied from the document, in a second batch under the same submission id.
A batch with nothing to carry is not sent.
Each component's tests in the first batch carry the cases and omittedCases of its tests entry, copied from the document.
An entry without cases uploads the same body as before.
Over 768 KiB of cases, the entry that lists the most loses its cases first, counted in its omittedCases, with a warning naming it.
A batch refused with 413 or 400 while it carries cases is posted again without them, with a warning naming the refusal.

Each dependency change in the second batch keeps the before and after states the document gives it: the licenses and the known vulnerabilities, each with its id and severity, and an empty state as empty.
A dependency change without a state uploads the same body as before the states existed.
A batch refused with 413 for its size while it carries states is posted again without them, with a warning that names the refusal.
A document's spec verification record and its declarations are each posted in a batch of their own under the run's submission id, copied from the document.
An empty declarations list is posted as an empty list.
A document without them sends no such batch.

Without a credential, with a document that does not parse or validate, or with a document whose subject names no numeric project id, it sends nothing and exits non-zero with a message that names the cause.
A refused run or batch exits non-zero with the route and the server's reason, and never prints the token;
a run opened again without its operational counts as refused only when that call is refused too.
Under --output=json a refused batch prints one failure result naming the run and what it stored.

With --sign-in, no token and no ID token exchange, the command uses the session putnami cloud login stored, refreshed when expired, and runs the same device sign-in when none exists, then uploads as that person: the run names the repository and no workspace, and Putnami Cloud opens the observed workspace in the person's organization.
With a token in PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, the upload names the repository too: an organization's ingest token needs it.
Without --sign-in, a token or the exchange, it refuses.

In a GitHub Actions job (GITHUB_ACTIONS true) with PUTNAMI_ORGANIZATION and no PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, it requests the job's ID token for the auth-server's base URL, exchanges it at the auth-server for client delivery-ingest and that organization_id, and uploads with the answered token, naming the repository, even with --sign-in.
An explicit PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN wins: no ID token is requested.

In a GitLab CI job (GITLAB_CI true) with PUTNAMI_ORGANIZATION and no PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, it reads the job's ID token from PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN, which the job's id_tokens declares with the auth-server's base URL as its audience, exchanges it at the auth-server for client delivery-ingest and that organization_id, and uploads with the answered token, naming the repository, even with --sign-in.
An explicit PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN wins: the ID token is not sent.
PUTNAMI_ORGANIZATION in a GitHub Actions job (GITHUB_ACTIONS true) without ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL or ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN sends nothing and names permissions id-token: write.
The auth-server's refusal for a repository the organization does not trust is named with the observation trust to add.
Any other failed request names the request and its reason. Each exits non-zero and prints no token.
PUTNAMI_ORGANIZATION in a GitLab CI job (GITLAB_CI true) without PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN sends nothing and names the id_tokens entry to declare, with the auth-server's base URL as aud.

A job of a GitLab instance other than gitlab.com (CI_SERVER_HOST) is told to set PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN. A PUTNAMI_ID_TOKEN whose iss is not https://gitlab.com, or with no aud exactly that base URL, is not sent.
The exchange's refusal of an untrusted project, worded as for a repository, names the trust to add.

requirements.text: The result carries data.reportUrl, the report URL Delivery answers when it opens the run, when that is an absolute https URL, and the summary line names it.

text: When a report batch answers level3Preview, the level 3 preview Delivery computes on the self-reported run, the result carries it as data.level3Preview beside data.reportUrl, as the last batch that answered one gave it.
A run whose batches answer none carries no data.level3Preview.
